examples.en: Mullet sashimi is delicious in winter.
I bought one mullet at the market.
A mullet jumped up at the river mouth.

examples.ko: 숭어는 바다와 강이 만나는 곳에서도 살아요.
examples.en: Mullet also live where the sea and a river meet.
I caught a mullet by fishing at the weekend.
Grilled mullet is tasty with just salt.

explain: 회나 구이로 먹는 생선이에요. 물 위로 잘 뛰어오르는 모습 때문에 속담에도 나와요.

phrases.example: 친구가 한다고 따라 하다니, 숭어가 뛰니까 망둥이도 뛴다더니 딱 그 말이네요.
phrases.en: Copying just because your friend does it—it's just like the saying 'when the mullet jumps, the goby jumps too.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 하니까 자기 형편은 생각하지 않고 무작정 따라 하는 사람을 놀릴 때 쓰는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb used to tease someone who blindly copies others without considering their own situation.

explain_en: It is a fish eaten as sashimi or grilled. Because it often leaps out of the water, it appears in a proverb.

examples.en: Braised monkfish is spicy and goes well with rice.
I bought one monkfish at the market.
Monkfish looks scary, but it tastes good.
I'm going to eat monkfish stew for dinner tonight.
The net was full of monkfish.
Do you know a restaurant that makes good monkfish dishes?

explain: 머리가 크고 입이 큰 바닷물고기예요. 한국에서는 매운 '아귀찜'이나 '아귀탕'으로 많이 먹어요. 같은 소리의 '아귀다툼'은 서로 헐뜯으며 다투는 모습인데, 이때 아귀는 불교에서 말하는 굶주린 귀신이라 물고기와 달라요.

phrases.en: On cold days I crave hot monkfish stew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아귀로 끓인 국물 요리예요. 아귀찜보다 국물이 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soup dish made with monkfish; it has more broth than 아귀찜.

phrases.example: 회사 근처에 맛있는 아귀찜 집이 있어요.
phrases.en: There's a tasty braised monkfish restaurant near my office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아귀찜을 파는 식당을 말해요. 식당을 소개할 때 '음식 이름 + 집'으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A restaurant that sells braised monkfish; Koreans often say 'dish name + 집' for a restaurant.

phrases.en: I tried a monkfish dish in Busan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아귀로 만든 음식을 모두 가리키는 말이에요. 찜, 탕 같은 이름을 모를 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A general term for dishes made with monkfish, usable when you don't know the specific name.

explain_en: It is a sea fish with a huge head and mouth. In Korea people mostly eat it as spicy 아귀찜 (braised) or 아귀탕 (stew). The word 아귀다툼 (a vicious squabble) uses a different 아귀, the hungry ghost in Buddhism, not the fish.

examples.ko: 퇴근하기 전에 쌀을 씻어서 안쳐 놨어요.
examples.en: Before leaving work, I washed the rice and put it on to cook.
I put the rice on in the pot and made side dishes.

examples.ko: 엄마가 밥을 안치는 동안 저는 상을 폈어요.
examples.en: While Mom put the rice on, I set out the table.
I'll put the rice on today.

examples.ko: 밥을 안친 지 십 분밖에 안 됐어요.
examples.en: It's only been ten minutes since I put the rice on.
I poured water to put the stew on in the pot.

explain: 밥이나 찌개, 떡을 만들려고 재료를 솥이나 냄비에 넣어 불 위에 올리는 것까지를 말해요. 요즘 대화에서는 '밥 올리다', '밥하다'라고 더 많이 말해요. '안쳐요', '안친', '안칠'처럼 활용하고 불규칙은 아니에요.

phrases.en: To prepare dinner, I put the rice on first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥을 하려고 솥에 쌀과 물을 넣어 불에 올리는 것을 말하는 대표 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The typical pairing for putting rice and water in the pot and setting it on the heat.
phrases.en_equiv: to put rice on to cook

phrases.en: Mom has already put the rice on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안치다와 같은 뜻으로 요즘 대화에서 더 자연스럽게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 안치다 but more natural in modern conversation.

phrases.en: After putting the rice on, I make the side dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순서를 말할 때 쓰는 연결 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to express sequence.

explain_en: It covers putting rice, stew or rice cake ingredients in a pot and setting it on the heat. In today's conversation people more often say '밥 올리다' or '밥하다'. It conjugates as '안쳐요', '안친', '안칠' and is not irregular.

examples.ko: 정월 대보름에는 약밥을 먹는 집이 있어요.
examples.en: Some families eat yakbap on the first full moon of the new year.

examples.ko: 약밥에 밤과 대추가 들어 있어서 달콤해요.
examples.en: The yakbap has chestnuts and jujubes in it, so it's sweet.
Yakbap stays chewy even when cold, so it's good for a lunchbox.
I learned how to make yakbap from my grandmother.

examples.ko: 약밥이 너무 달아서 차와 같이 먹었어요.
examples.en: The yakbap was too sweet, so I ate it with tea.

examples.ko: 시장에서 약밥 한 팩을 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I bought a pack of yakbap at the market.

explain: '약식'이라고도 불러요. 보통 흰밥과 달리 달고 쫀득해서 밥보다는 간식이나 명절 음식으로 먹어요.

phrases.en: Yaksik is sweet and chewy.
phrases.nuance_ko: '약밥'과 같은 음식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same food as yakbap.

phrases.en: My grandmother makes yakbap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 직접 만든다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone makes the food themselves.

phrases.en: Please have a piece of yakbap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 권할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for offering the food to someone.

explain_en: It is also called '약식'. Unlike plain white rice it is sweet and chewy, so people eat it more as a snack or holiday food than as a meal.

en: to be spicy; to be hot

examples.en: Today I want to eat something with a spicy, hearty broth.

examples.ko: 순두부찌개에 청양고추를 썰어 넣으니 얼큰한 맛이 두 배가 됐어요.
examples.en: After I sliced chili peppers into the soft tofu stew, the spicy kick doubled.

examples.ko: 이 짬뽕은 국물이 얼큰해서 속이 풀려요.
examples.en: This jjamppong has a spicy broth that soothes my stomach.
I ate kimchi stew that was boiled spicy and rich.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 얼큰한 찌개가 생각나요.
examples.en: On rainy days I think of a spicy stew.

examples.ko: 얼큰한 맛에 땀이 났지만 계속 먹었어요.
examples.en: The spiciness made me sweat, but I kept eating.

explain: 그냥 매운 것이 아니라 맵고 시원하게 느껴지는 국물 맛에 주로 써요. 찌개, 탕, 국 같은 국물 요리에 잘 어울리고, 매운 과자나 매운 소스에는 보통 '맵다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날에는 얼큰한 국물이 생각나요.
phrases.en: On rainy days I crave a spicy, hot broth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '얼큰하다'는 국물과 가장 잘 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Broth' is the most natural partner for 얼큰하다.

phrases.en: This kimchi stew is really spicy and warming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 음식 맛을 말할 때 쓰는 기본 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic polite form for describing how a dish tastes.

phrases.example: 이 찌개는 얼큰하지 않아서 아이도 먹을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: This stew isn't spicy, so even kids can eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맵고 시원한 맛이 없다고 할 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying the dish lacks that spicy, refreshing kick.

explain_en: It is not just for anything spicy, but mainly for the spicy-yet-refreshing taste of a soup broth. It suits soup dishes like stews and '탕', while for spicy snacks or sauces people normally use '맵다'.

t90.ax: On rainy days I think of a spicy stew.

examples.ko: 어머니가 완자를 부쳐서 도시락에 넣어 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother pan-fried wanja and put them in my lunchbox.

examples.ko: 명절에는 우리 집에서 완자를 꼭 만들어요.
examples.en: At the holidays, we always make wanja at our house.
Wanja are made by shaping meat into little rounds.

examples.ko: 이 완자는 간이 딱 맞아서 맛있어요.
examples.en: These meatballs are seasoned just right, so they're delicious.
If you add tofu to the meatball mixture, it turns out soft.

examples.ko: 아이들이 완자를 너무 좋아해서 금방 없어졌어요.
examples.en: The kids love meatballs so much that they were gone in no time.

explain: 고기나 두부를 동그랗게 빚어 부치거나 삶아 먹는 음식이에요. 집에서는 '동그랑땡'이라고도 많이 불러요. 국에 넣은 건 '완자탕'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I shaped meatballs together with my family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반죽을 동그랗게 만들 때 '빚다'를 쓰며, 완자를 만드는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 빚다 is used for shaping dough into rounds; the most common way to say making meatballs.

phrases.example: 추운 날에는 따뜻한 완자탕이 먹고 싶어요.
phrases.en: On cold days, I want to eat warm meatball soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완자를 국에 넣어 끓인 음식을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a dish with meatballs boiled in soup.

phrases.en: Donggeurangttaeng is the same kind of food as wanja.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 많이 부르는 같은 음식의 다른 이름으로, 말할 때 더 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Another name for the same dish used at home, more casual to say.

explain_en: It is food made by shaping meat or tofu into rounds and pan-frying or boiling them. At home, many people also call it '동그랑땡'. When it is put in soup, it is called '완자탕'.

examples.en: This steak is full of juices.

examples.ko: 육즙을 살리려면 센 불에서 먼저 구워요.
examples.en: To keep the juices in, sear it first over high heat.
When I bit into the dumpling, juice flowed out.
I ate a juicy hamburger.

examples.ko: 고기를 잠깐 두어야 육즙이 안에 남아요.
examples.en: Let the meat rest a bit so the juices stay inside.
Juicy meat gets softer the more you chew.

explain: 고기에서 나오는 국물이고, 맛있다는 칭찬에 자주 나와요. '육즙이 풍부하다', '육즙이 흐르다'처럼 써요. 과일은 '과즙'이라고 하고, 고기나 뼈를 끓여 낸 국물은 '육수'라서 달라요.

phrases.en: The meat in this burger is very juicy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기가 맛있다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common way to praise tasty meat.
phrases.en_equiv: to be rich in meat juices

phrases.en: Juices ran out when I cut the meat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고기를 자르거나 씹을 때 국물이 나오는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It describes juice coming out when meat is cut or chewed.

phrases.example: 고기를 너무 오래 굽지 말고 육즙을 살리세요.
phrases.en: Don't grill the meat too long, and keep the juices in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리할 때 국물이 빠지지 않게 한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means cooking so the juices do not escape.

explain_en: It is the juice that comes out of meat and often shows up in praise: '육즙이 풍부하다', '육즙이 흐르다'. Fruit juice is '과즙', and broth boiled from meat or bones is '육수', a different word.

examples.en: I mash the boiled potatoes with a fork.
Mash the banana, then mix it with milk.
I crushed the tofu by hand and put it in.

examples.ko: 마늘을 칼로 으깨면 향이 더 진해요.
examples.en: If you crush garlic with a knife, the aroma gets stronger.
The child crushed the snack and spilled it on the floor.
I made a tasty snack with mashed sweet potato.

explain: 단단하지 않은 것을 눌러서 형태가 없게 만들 때 써요. 요리에서 '감자, 바나나, 두부, 마늘'과 자주 같이 써요. '부수다'는 단단한 것이 깨질 때, '으깨다'는 부드러운 것을 눌러서 뭉갤 때라서 달라요.

phrases.en: I added butter to the mashed potatoes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 이름이나 재료를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for dish names or ingredients.

phrases.en: I mash the tofu and mix it with vegetables.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 순서를 말할 때 '-아/어서'로 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Linked with -아/어서 when describing cooking steps.

phrases.en: The banana got mushy because it was too ripe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 저절로 눌려서 뭉개졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something gets crushed on its own.

explain_en: It is used when you press something soft until it loses its shape. In cooking it often goes with potatoes, bananas, tofu and garlic. '부수다' is for breaking something hard, while '으깨다' is for squashing something soft.

t90.ax: I mash the boiled potatoes with a fork.

examples.ko: 아기가 이유식을 잘 먹어서 정말 다행이에요.
examples.en: I'm so relieved that the baby eats baby food well.

examples.ko: 아기에게 이유식을 먹이는 데 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Feeding the baby weaning food takes a long time.

examples.ko: 저는 주말마다 이유식 재료를 사러 마트에 가요.
examples.en: Every weekend I go to the supermarket to buy ingredients for baby food.

examples.ko: 요즘은 시판 이유식도 종류가 아주 많아요.
examples.en: These days there are many kinds of store-bought baby food too.

examples.ko: 이유식을 먹일 때마다 아기가 자꾸 뱉어요.
examples.en: Every time I feed the baby solids, the baby keeps spitting them out.
At first, we start with baby food made from rice.

explain: 젖이나 분유만 먹던 아기가 밥으로 넘어가는 중간 단계의 음식이라 육아 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '이유식을 만들다', '이유식을 먹이다'처럼 쓰고, 그다음 단계 음식은 '유아식'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Every weekend I make baby food for my baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 육아 이야기에서 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase in talk about raising a baby.

phrases.example: 아기가 육 개월이 되어서 이유식을 시작했어요.
phrases.en: My baby turned six months old, so we started solid food.
phrases.nuance_ko: 젖이나 분유에서 밥으로 넘어가는 시기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time when a baby moves from milk to solid food.

phrases.en: I bought ingredients for baby food at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유식을 만들 때 쓰는 재료를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the ingredients used to make baby food.

explain_en: This is the in-between food for a baby moving from milk or formula to regular meals, so it comes up a lot in parenting talk. It goes with '이유식을 만들다' and '이유식을 먹이다'. The next stage of food is called '유아식'.

examples.en: He is learning baking skills.

examples.ko: 제빵 학원에 다닌 지 석 달이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been three months since I started going to a baking school.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 좋은 제빵 재료만 써요.
examples.en: This shop uses only good baking ingredients.

examples.ko: 제빵사가 되려면 어떤 공부를 해야 해요?
examples.en: What do I need to study to become a baker?

examples.ko: 제빵 대회에서 우리 학교가 일등을 했어요.
examples.en: Our school took first place at the baking competition.
A nutty bread smell is coming from the bakery room.

explain: 혼자 쓰기보다 '제빵 기술', '제빵사', '제빵 학원'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요. 과자와 케이크를 만드는 일은 '제과'라서 합쳐서 '제과제빵'이라고 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: My dream is to become a baker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빵을 만드는 일을 직업으로 하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a person who makes bread as a profession.

phrases.en: I study baking and confectionery at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과자·케이크를 만드는 '제과'와 빵을 만드는 '제빵'을 합쳐서 한 단어처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combines 제과 (pastry/confectionery) and 제빵 (bread) into one phrase.

phrases.en: I want to get a baking certificate this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제빵' 뒤에 말을 붙여 쓰는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical collocation where 제빵 is followed by another noun.

explain_en: It is rarely used alone; it usually takes a following word, as in '제빵 기술', '제빵사' and '제빵 학원'. Making cookies and cakes is '제과', so people often say '제과제빵' together.

examples.ko: 젤라틴을 따뜻한 물에 녹여서 푸딩을 만들어요.
examples.en: I dissolve gelatin in warm water to make pudding.
Gelatin is obtained from animal bones and skin.

examples.ko: 채식하는 사람은 젤라틴이 든 과자를 피해요.
examples.en: People who eat vegetarian avoid snacks that contain gelatin.

examples.ko: 젤라틴 가루 대신 한천을 써도 돼요.
examples.en: You can use agar instead of gelatin powder.
If you set it with gelatin, the mousse cake becomes firm.

examples.ko: 젤라틴만으로는 맛이 안 나서 과일즙을 넣어요.
examples.en: Gelatin alone has no flavor, so I add fruit juice.

explain: '젤리'는 만들어진 간식이고, '젤라틴'은 그것을 굳히는 재료예요. 식물로 만든 비슷한 재료로는 '한천'이 있어요. 식품 성분표에서도 자주 볼 수 있는 말이에요.

phrases.example: 젤라틴 가루를 물에 넣고 천천히 저어 주세요.
phrases.en: Put the gelatin powder in water and stir slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '젤라틴'이 가루 모양일 때 쓰는 말로, 요리법에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for gelatin in powder form; common in recipes.

phrases.en: I hardened juice with gelatin and made jelly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '젤라틴'이 무엇을 굳히는 재료라는 쓰임을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows gelatin's role as a setting agent.

phrases.en: This snack contains gelatin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식품 성분을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about food ingredients.

explain_en: '젤리' is the finished snack, while '젤라틴' is the ingredient that sets it. A similar plant-based ingredient is '한천' (agar). You can also see it on food ingredient labels.

examples.en: I braise mackerel together with radish.
I braised the potatoes in soy sauce.
It is a side dish of anchovies braised sweet.

examples.ko: 국물이 거의 없어질 때까지 조려야 해요.
examples.en: You have to braise it until almost no broth is left.

examples.ko: 엄마는 갈치를 조릴 때 고춧가루를 넣어요.
examples.en: When my mom braises hairtail, she adds chili powder.

examples.ko: 불을 줄이고 천천히 조리면 맛이 배요.
examples.en: If you lower the heat and braise slowly, the flavor soaks in.

explain: '생선조림', '감자조림'처럼 이 동사에서 나온 요리 이름이 많아요. 음식은 보통 '조리다'를 쓰고, 마음은 꼭 '졸이다'를 써서 '마음을 졸이다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I ate braised fish with rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ' 형태로 음식 이름 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a food name to describe it as braised.

phrases.en: I am braising potatoes now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식을 만드는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used while the food is being cooked.

phrases.en: If you braise it a long time on low heat, it tastes good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요리 방법을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when explaining how to cook.

explain_en: Many dish names come from this verb, such as '생선조림' and '감자조림'. For food, use '조리다'; for nervous feelings you need a different verb, '졸이다', as in '마음을 졸이다' (be on tenterhooks).

examples.ko: 주요리는 소고기와 생선 중에서 고를 수 있어요.
examples.en: For the main dish, you can choose between beef and fish.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 주요리보다 후식이 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: At this restaurant the dessert is tastier than the main dish.

examples.ko: 주요리가 나오기 전에 샐러드를 먼저 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate a salad first before the main dish came out.
I prepared a chicken dish as the main course.

examples.ko: 주요리 양이 많아서 사이드는 하나만 시켰어요.
examples.en: The main dish was big, so I ordered only one side.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁 주요리는 제가 직접 만들게요.
examples.en: I'll make tonight's main dish myself.

explain: '메인 요리'라고도 해요. 코스 요리에서는 앞에 나오는 '전채', 뒤에 나오는 '후식'과 순서로 같이 기억하면 쉬워요.

phrases.en: I'll have the steak as my main dish.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주요리'와 같은 뜻이고, 식당에서는 외래어로도 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same, and restaurants often use this loanword.

phrases.en: Please choose your main dish first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 코스에서 선택해야 할 때 '고르다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'choose' when you pick from a course menu.

phrases.en: Fish is served as the main dish today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇이 주요리인지 말할 때 '-로'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-로' to say what the main dish is.
phrases.en_equiv: be served as the main dish

explain_en: It is also called '메인 요리'. In a course meal, it is easy to remember in order with the starter '전채' before it and the dessert '후식' after it.

examples.en: It's my habit to snack while reading.
Even though I've had dinner, I keep wanting to snack.
Don't snack. Have your meal first.

examples.ko: 오후 내내 주전부리해서 배가 안 고파요.
examples.en: I snacked all afternoon, so I'm not hungry.
The kids snacked while watching the movie.
We chatted in the park while snacking.

explain: 식사가 아니라 끼니 사이에 이것저것 입에 넣는 것을 말해요. '간식을 먹다'보다 가벼운 느낌이고, '군것질하다'와 거의 같아요. '주전부리를 하다'처럼 띄어서 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I snack while watching a movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: '주전부리하다'를 띄어서 쓴 말로, 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spaced version of 주전부리하다 with the same meaning.

phrases.en: My younger sibling often snacks in front of the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 같은 뜻이고, 일상 대화에서 더 흔히 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning and a bit more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: Please don't snack before dinner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간식을 먹지 말라고 부드럽게 말할 때 쓰는 부정 명령이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite negative command telling someone not to snack.

explain_en: It means munching on this and that between meals rather than eating a proper meal. It feels lighter than '간식을 먹다' and is nearly the same as '군것질하다'. It can also be written as '주전부리를 하다'.

examples.en: I put egg strips on top of the spicy noodles.

examples.ko: 어머니가 노른자와 흰자를 따로 지단으로 부치셨어요.
examples.en: My mother fried the yolk and the white separately into thin egg sheets.
Egg garnish looks nice when it is cut thin.
Kimbap is softer when you add egg strips.
Banquet noodles usually come with egg strips on top.
Please teach me how to make egg garnish.

explain: 국수, 떡국, 잡채, 김밥에 올리거나 넣어서 색을 내는 데 많이 써요. 노른자로 만들면 노란색, 흰자로 만들면 흰색 지단이 돼요. 계란말이나 계란프라이와는 다른 음식이에요.

phrases.en: I fried thin egg sheets with eggs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지단을 만드는 일은 '부치다'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Making 지단 is expressed with 부치다.

phrases.en: I cut the egg sheet into thin strips and put it on top.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부친 지단을 가늘게 썰어 음식 위에 올릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for slicing the fried egg thinly to garnish a dish.

phrases.en: I put yellow and white egg strips on the tteokguk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 노른자 지단과 흰자 지단을 같이 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The name for yolk and white egg strips together.

explain_en: It adds color to noodles, rice cake soup, japchae, and kimbap. Yolk makes yellow strips and egg white makes white ones. It is a different dish from '계란말이' or '계란프라이'.
